title: Private Health Insurance (National Joint Replacement Register Levy) Amendment Bill 2025
short_title: Private Health Insurance (National Joint Replacement Register Levy) Amendment Bill 2025

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would change how responsibility for paying the national joint replacement registry levy is identified, allowing the liable person to be specified through rules.
This would allow liability to follow changes in responsibility for listed medical devices over time, rather than relying solely on the person who obtained the initial listing.
The bill would validate earlier levy collections on the specified basis and commence on the 14th day after Royal Assent, allowing time to update the rules.
changes: The levy legislation's definition of sponsor would be removed.
The definition referring to medical devices and human tissue products rules would be replaced with a clearer version.
New arrangements would apply to levies imposed from commencement, including where calculations refer to earlier events.
summary.affected: People responsible for relevant listed medical devices who would be liable to pay the levy are affected.

speeches.speaker: Rebecca White
speeches.brief: Moved the Private Health Insurance (National Joint Replacement Register Levy) Amendment Bill 2025, allowing rules to identify the person responsible for the levy over time and validating past levy collections.

speeches.speaker: Anne Ruston
speeches.brief: Supported the Private Health Insurance (National Joint Replacement Register Levy) Amendment Bill 2025, saying it would clarify levy responsibility and validate past collections so the registry could continue collecting and analysing joint-replacement data; also criticised hospital funding and aged-care delivery, including delays in releasing home-care packages.

speeches.speaker: Sue Lines
speeches.brief: Asked that the second reading amendment moved by Senator Ruston to the Private Health Insurance (National Joint Replacement Register Levy) Amendment Bill 2025 be agreed to.
